newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Guiana "arsonist" says police pressured him to talk.
newsitem.headline: Guiana "arsonist" says police pressured him to talk.

text.p: One of 11 suspected arsonists in French Guiana said on Sunday police had pressured him into making false statements implicating leading separatist activists.

Daniel Prevot, at 22 the youngest member of the 11 who have been charged with with setting fire to the home of the French territory's state prosecutor during riots last November, said police used intimidation to secure false statements.

Prevot, who has been released from pre-trial detention, told state radio police took him from his home early last April and questioned him about the blaze -- an incident he said he had not been aware of.

"I was put under pressure and intimidated into making false statements. After making these false statements I retracted because what I said was not true and I could not implicate and condemn people since I was not there and had seen nothing," he said.

The 11 were arrested in April and charged with arson and violence against a magistrate. They were transferred to the French Caribbean island of Martinique to allow a prosecutor not personally involved in the incident to proceed with prosecution.

Their arrests led to a new wave of riots in French Guiana's capital Cayenne during three nights last month. Paramilitary police flown in from France clashed with hooded rioters firing hunting rifles and hurling petrol bombs.
Officials said 11 police were injured, ten by gunfire. A bystander lost an eye when a projectile exploded in his face.
The riots have shattered French Guiana's tranquil facade and laid bare economic, political and social woes.
French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent mainland territory in the Western Hemisphere.
It lags behind mainland France in housing, education and health. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 24 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
